description: update_email() switched from returning False to raising, breaking its caller.
why_wrong: app/api.py's handle_update_email() checks the boolean return to produce a 400 response. It has no try/except, so invalid input now propagates an uncaught exception instead of a 400. The function's new behaviour is internally coherent -- the defect is only visible from the caller, in another file.
diff:
--- a/app/services/user.py
+++ b/app/services/user.py
@@ -25,10 +25,10 @@
 def update_email(user_id: int, new_email: str) -> bool:
     """Change a user's email. Returns False when the user or email is invalid."""
     if not is_valid_email(new_email):
-        return False
+        raise ValueError("invalid email")
     user = get_user(user_id)
     if user is None:
-        return False
+        raise LookupError("no such user")
     user["email"] = new_email
     return True
